title: A Starry Gateway
caption: The Milky Way framed by the entrance to Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Milky Way streaks overhead, where glowing gas, dark dust and countless sparkling stars stand out vividly against the blacker sky around them. In the foreground, the entrance to ESO's Paranal Observatory frames the plane of our galaxy.

Paranal is ESO's flagship observatory and one of the best places in the world for looking at the sky. It sits more than 2600 meters above sea level in Chile's Atacama Desert, well away from the light pollution that human settlements produce.

The glowing band is our galaxy seen edge-on from within. Stars, glowing gas and lanes of dust all lie in a flattened disc, and we see that disc as a stripe across the sky. From a site this dark, the contrast between the bright star clouds and the dark dust is easy to capture, which is exactly why astronomers value such locations.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye can, so the gas, dust and stars of the Milky Way look far more vivid here than they would in person.
